clue.text: Jam? In tagliatelle?

parts.note: read as wordplay: the word tail written backwards, which sits inside the pasta's name as LIAT

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether a jam has found its way into a plate of pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, split as TAIL BACK, is an instruction whose result (LIAT) is found in tagLIATelle. 'Jam' is the traffic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailback is a long queue of stationary traffic, which is exactly what a traffic jam produces.

clue.text: Where you can find venue with beers to store letters of faithful followers

parts.note: VENUE is the answer at 12 across in this grid, so you find it at twelve

indicators.note: to store says the beers hold the letters word inside them

parts.note: ales are beers
post means letters, the mail

explanation.surface: Pub storage talk: a venue with beers that also keeps the post for devoted fans.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part refers to this grid itself: the answer VENUE is entered at 12.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twelve Apostles were the disciples chosen by Jesus, his most devoted inner circle.

clue.text: They say you again got entangled with an American native

indicators.note: got entangled says the letters are knotted into a fresh order
they say marks a word as heard, so you is taken as the letter that sounds like it

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone you met twice got caught up with a Native American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' turns 'you' into U; 'got entangled' rearranges U + AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large lizard native to Central and South America.

clue.text: Doctrine about Caesar, oddly not shown in sculptor's work

indicators.note: about says the doctrine word goes around the kept letters

parts.note: a belief is a doctrine or tenet

indicators.note: oddly not shown drops the odd-placed letters of Caesar, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A creed concerning Caesar, partly hidden, appears in a sculptor's carving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly not shown' hides the odd letters of Caesar, leaving the even ones, ASR, which 'about' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bas-relief is low-relief sculpture, with figures standing slightly out from a flat background.

clue.text: Timekeepers extremely eager, but not this one

definitions.text: Timekeepers extremely eager, but not this one

parts.note: a clock and a watch are both timekeepers

indicators.note: extremely takes the outermost letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Most timekeepers are keen, but this one is not.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a clock-watcher keeps an eye on the time and is anything but eager.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock-watcher is an employee who constantly checks the time, impatient to stop working.

clue.text: Old citizen is a hard worker

definitions.meaning: to 'work like a ...' is to work very hard, so a ... is a tireless worker

explanation.surface: Someone describes an elderly resident as a diligent labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy's inhabitants were Trojans, and the idiom 'work like a Trojan' makes the same word mean a tireless labourer.

clue.text: In Singapore, I'm searching for a source of fizz

indicators.note: in says the answer is contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A traveller in Singapore hunts for somewhere selling sparkling drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Reims is the city at the heart of the Champagne region of France, home of sparkling wine.

clue.text: Risk of standard diet originally eaten by kangaroo, after a change of heart

indicators.note: eaten by says the standard and diet pieces go inside the kangaroo word
a change of heart says the two central letters of the kangaroo word switch places

parts.note: a joey is a young kangaroo
par is a standard, as in 'up to par'

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letter of diet

explanation.surface: A kangaroo, eating its usual diet, takes a risk after changing its mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a change of heart' swaps the two central letters of the young kangaroo, giving JEOY, which 'eaten by' then opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeopardy means danger or exposure to loss, as in 'putting a job in jeopardy'.

clue.text: Half past seven in the evening is a time of depression

definitions.text: Half past seven in the evening
definitions.meaning: on the 24-hour clock half past seven in the evening is 19:30
1930 falls in the Great Depression of the 1930s

explanation.surface: Someone declares that half past seven each evening is when their mood sinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a clock time it is 19:30; read as a year it falls in the Great Depression.

clue.text: Paint nudism au naturel, finally implicated in recurrent commotion

indicators.note: implicated in means caught up within, so the picked letters go inside the other piece
recurrent is taken as running back, so the commotion word is read backwards

parts.note: noise is a commotion or din

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: An instruction to depict nudism in the raw ends up embroiled in a recurring fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paint' looks like a verb but is the noun. 'recurrent' gives ESION, and 'implicated in' sets the three final letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is the common water-based paint used on interior walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Refuse to acknowledge one's outwardly depressed

indicators.note: outwardly says the depressed word sits on the outside, wrapping the other piece

parts.note: depressed means down, low in spirits
one is I, and the 's stands for is, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone declines to admit they are feeling low on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' wraps the depressed word round 'one's', read as one (I) plus the 's (is).
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone or something is to deny any connection with it, refusing to acknowledge it as yours.

clue.text: Coy orphan, age uncertain, a subject for deep study

indicators.note: uncertain suggests the letters are not settled and can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shy orphan of unknown age is the subject of a serious study.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanography is the science of the seas, so it is literally the study of the deep.

clue.text: Street's not a place for events and functions

indicators.note: not says the following word is to be left out of the street word

parts.note: an avenue is a street, the 's linking it to what follows

explanation.surface: A road, we are told, is no place to hold parties and receptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' removes the A from AVENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is the location where a gathering such as a concert, match or reception takes place.

clue.text: Old motorbikes feature thrills with skill rounding junction

indicators.note: rounding says the skill word comes round after the junction letter, closing off the answer

parts.note: kicks are thrills, as in 'doing it for kicks'
T is a T-junction, so the letter stands for junction
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Excitement and know-how are needed to get round a road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounding' brings skill round after the junction letter to close the answer; the T is not inside the thrills.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick-start is the foot-operated lever used to fire up the engine on older motorcycles before electric starters.

clue.text: Very well and appropriate baffle, as if playing inside

parts.note: fit means appropriate or suitable

indicators.note: inside says the rearranged letters go within the baffle word

parts.note: to addle is to confuse or baffle

indicators.note: playing suggests the words as if being toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A suitable acoustic baffle appears to be playing inside a sound system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' turns AS IF into SAFI, and 'inside' sets it after the first letter of the baffle word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'fit as a fiddle' means in excellent health, in perfect condition.

clue.text: Where to share pictures of fashionable males

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a stag and a ram are both male animals

explanation.surface: A tip on the best place to post photos of trendy men.
explanation.definitionFit: Instagram is a social media app built around posting and sharing photos and videos.

clue.text: See 1
Bravo for Mike in rush for game

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of the other within the rush word

parts.note: to scramble is to rush or hurry
Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M
Bravo is the NATO alphabet word for B

explanation.surface: Swapping one call sign for another during a hectic dash to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' replaces the M in SCRAMBLE with B.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is the board game in which players build crossing words from lettered tiles.

clue.text: You'll find that to the west of Mexico father cooks first, provided with tiny capacity oven

definitions.text: You'll find that to the west of Mexico

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of cooks

parts.note: if means provided, as in 'provided that'
1cc, one cubic centimetre, is a tiny volume
an oast is a kiln or oven for drying hops

explanation.surface: A recipe line: Dad cooks first, using a minuscule oven.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of 1cc is read as I. An oast is a hop-drying kiln, familiar in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexico's western shore faces the Pacific Ocean, so that coastline lies to the west of the country.

clue.text: Order giving rise to rubbish joke

indicators.note: rise, in a down clue, says the pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish or tasteless goods
to kid is to joke or tease

explanation.surface: A command that sparked a silly gag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' reverses TAT + KID in this down clue to give DIK + TAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a decree or command imposed without consultation, an order from above.

clue.text: See 8
Piddling half-pint?

definitions.meaning: a half-pint of beer is literally a ..., the question mark flagging the playful reading

explanation.definitionFit: Small beer is an idiom for trivial matters, while a half-pint is a small measure of ale.

clue.text: Return visit to wrap one's flower

indicators.note: to wrap says the reversed visit word goes around the one
return says the visit word is turned back to front

parts.note: a call is a short visit
one is I, the 's tying it to the rest

explanation.surface: A return visit with a bunch of flowers wrapped as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns CALL into LLAC; 'to wrap' puts I inside: L-I-LAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a shrub with fragrant purple or white blossom clusters, a common garden flower.

clue.text: Primarily austere, mostly illiberal, quiet sect

indicators.note: primarily tells us to take the opening letters of the next three words

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A description of a religious group: stern, largely intolerant and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface doubles as a description of the sect, so the whole clue paints the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a Protestant community in America known for plain dress and avoiding modern technology.

clue.text: Liable to change

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters of the first word to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A brief description of something unstable.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of LIABLE is itself an example of the letters changing.
explanation.definitionFit: Labile is a technical term in chemistry and psychology for something unstable or readily altered.

clue.text: Driver for pointless proportionate representation

indicators.note: representation is read as re-presentation, a fresh arrangement of the remaining letters

parts.note: pointless means without point, so those letters are removed from the long word

explanation.surface: A call for proportional representation, but one that has no point.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P, O, I, N, T out of PROPORTIONATE, leaving RPORTOAE, and rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator is someone who drives or works a machine, such as a crane or train operator.

clue.text: Hokusai's fifth boat illustration

indicators.note: fifth picks out the fifth letter of the artist's name

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: An art lover admires the fifth boat picture by the Japanese master Hokusai.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing, a quick illustration made before a finished picture.

clue.text: Yet my Mrs may be fearful of Tyger's appearance

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A husband suspects his wife fears the striped look of a tiger.
explanation.walkthrough: Blake's poem 'The Tyger' asks what could 'frame thy fearful symmetry'; the definition borrows that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Blake describes the tiger's balanced, mirror-image markings and form as its 'fearful symmetry'.
